title: Compactly supported direct image commutes with extension of coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $X$, $Y$, and $\bar X$ are separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms. Let $f:X\to Y$ have a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$, where $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ is open and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ is proper. Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by a power of $\ell$.

Use the ordinary uncompleted module derived categories and constant coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for the full subcategory with bounded, intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Write $K_B=K\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ with its $B_T$-action as in [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], and $Rf_{!,R}=R\bar f_{*,R}j_{!,R}$, with extension by zero as in [def-weil-extension-by-zero].

For $M\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ the canonical coefficient comparison is an isomorphism, natural in $M$, in $\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$:
$$
b_{A,B}(M):(Rf_{!,A}M)_B=(R\bar f_{*,A}j_{!,A}M)\otimes^L_{A_Y}B_Y
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar f_{*,B}j_{!,B}(M\otimes^L_{A_X}B_X)=Rf_{!,B}(M_B).
$$
Here the proper comparison is the $B$-linear adjoint transpose of the $A$-counit after extension of scalars, followed by the canonical extension-by-zero tensor comparison; the derived adjunctions are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. There is no flatness or finite projective dimension hypothesis on $B$ over $A$.

For every further homomorphism $B\to C$ of finite commutative $\ell$-primary rings, the comparison for $A\to C$ satisfies
$$
b_{A,C}(M)\circ\alpha_{Rf_{!,A}M}
=Rf_{!,C}(\alpha_M)\circ b_{B,C}(M_B)\circ(b_{A,B}(M))_C,
$$
where $\alpha_K:(K_B)_C\xrightarrow{\sim}K_C$ is the associativity isomorphism of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor].

proof.text:
Put $p=\bar f$, and let $T_T^{A,B}$ denote scalar extension on a scheme $T$. Pullback carries constant $B$ to constant $B$ by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Its derived tensor compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives a canonical identification $p_B^*T_Y^{A,B}\simeq T_{\bar X}^{A,B}p_A^*$; this is $B$-linear, since on tensor representatives its map preserves the right $B$-factor. For $N\in D(\bar X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ define
$$\gamma_N^{A,B}:T_Y^{A,B}Rp_*^A N\longrightarrow Rp_*^B T_{\bar X}^{A,B}N$$
by the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with transpose
$$p_B^*T_Y^{A,B}Rp_*^A N\simeq T_{\bar X}^{A,B}p_A^*Rp_*^A N\xrightarrow{T^{A,B}(\varepsilon_N^A)}T_{\bar X}^{A,B}N.$$
Thus, under this pullback identification, its defining identity is $\varepsilon^B_{TN}\,p_B^*(\gamma_N^{A,B})=T^{A,B}(\varepsilon_N^A)$. This constructs an actual $B$-linear map, without an assumption on the Tor dimension of $B/A$.

First construct the coefficient comparison as a morphism of $B$-complexes. Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to M$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The ordinary sheaf identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], for the open object $X$ of $\bar X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (whose localized-site identification is part of [def-weil-extension-by-zero]), gives $(j_!G)\otimes Q\simeq j_!(G\otimes j^*Q)$. It extends to total tensor complexes: $j_!$ preserves direct sums because it is a left adjoint [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. For any acyclic complex $Q$, $j^*Q$ is acyclic by exact pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], then $P\otimes j^*Q$ is acyclic by K-flatness, and $j_!(P\otimes j^*Q)$ is acyclic by exactness of $j_!$. Hence $j_!P$ is K-flat. The same identity on sheaves shows each $j_!P^i$ is flat, since both $j^*$ and $j_!$ are exact. Thus scalar extension on the two sides is computed by $j_!P\otimes_A B$ and $j_!^B(P\otimes_A B)$. Their termwise tensor comparison is $B$-linear (it preserves multiplication on the right $B$-factor), and is an isomorphism by the cited ordinary identity. It yields the canonical
$$e_M^{A,B}:T_{\bar X}^{A,B}j_!^A M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^B T_X^{A,B}M.$$
After restriction of scalars, this is the derived open tensor comparison [lem-trf-open-tensor]; compatibility of $j_!$ with restriction of scalars is included in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Its restriction to $X$ is the tensor identity. Define
$$b_{A,B}(M)=Rp_*^B(e_M^{A,B})\circ\gamma_{j_!^AM}^{A,B}.$$
These canonical derived comparisons are natural in $M$, without making a functorial choice of the resolution.

proof.text:
The arbitrary-finite-ring equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] supplies a bounded constructible etale $A$-complex $L$ with $
u_X^*L\simeq M$. Let $K=j_!^{\mathrm{et},A}L$. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $K$ bounded. The sheaf comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] extends termwise to complexes: both extension-by-zero functors and $
u^*$ are exact, so the sheaf isomorphism gives a complex isomorphism and survives localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Hence $
u_{ ar X}^*K\simeq N:=j_!^A M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], this also identifies $
u_{ ar X}^*(K\otimes_A^L B_{ ar X,\mathrm{et}})$ with $N\otimes_A^L B_{ ar X}$. The latter is bounded: Step 2 identifies its underlying $A$-complex with that of $j_!^B M_B$, and $M_B$ is bounded by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Exactness and the sheaf unit in [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] reflect vanishing of every cohomology sheaf: $H^i(
u^*E)=
u^*H^i(E)$ and $H^i(E)\simeq
u_*
u^*H^i(E)$. Thus $K\otimes_A^L B_{ ar X,\mathrm{et}}$ is bounded as well. Both etale arguments needed below therefore lie in $D^+$; no fully faithful comparison is applied to an unbounded-below tensor.

source.place: Tags 09AK, 09AL; lemma-compare-constructible-derived; jshriek comparison and exactness

proof.text: The schemes $\bar X,Y$ and $p$ satisfy the finite-type-over-a-field hypotheses of [lem-kun-0f10]. By its clause (1) and [def-kun-cd] there is one $c\geq0$ killing $R^qp_*$ on every torsion abelian etale sheaf for $q>c$. This is also a uniform bound for etale $A$-module sheaves, as follows. Resolve such a sheaf $F$ by injective $A$-module sheaves, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], which also gives enough injectives for the abelian sheaf category. Forgetting the action preserves exactness, and every term is $p_*$-acyclic as an abelian sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-direct-image-acyclic]. The acyclic-resolution criterion, clause (2) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qp_*^A F$ with $R^qp_*F$. The latter vanishes for $q>c$, since $F$ is killed by a power of $\ell$. Forgetting a module action reflects the zero object, proving the required module-sheaf bound for all $F$.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd (1); module-versus-abelian acyclicity: sites-cohomology.tex Tags 03FD and 072W

proof.text:
A finite commutative ring $A$ is Noetherian: its ideals form a finite set, so an ascending chain stabilizes. The finite set underlying $B$ generates it as an $A$-module, giving a finite free surjection $A^r\twoheadrightarrow B$; its kernel is a finite set because $A^r$ is finite, so it too has a finite generating set. This is a finite presentation of $B$ over $A$. Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] to the etale map $p$, coefficient ring $A$, the uniform bound $c$ from Step 4, bounded-above complex $K$ from Step 3, and constant finitely presented $A$-module $B$. It gives invertibility of the specified counit projection
$$\pi_K:Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}^A K\otimes_A^L B_{Y,\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}^A(K\otimes_A^L B_{\bar X,\mathrm{et}}).$$
This is precisely the finite-free-resolution/finite-window tool of the blueprint's Steps 2–3. Its statement imposes neither finite projective dimension of $B$ nor a bounded constructible flat model for $K$.

source.place: Steps 2–3, finite-free terms and finite windows, specialized through the existing general etale projection lemma

proof.text:
We check that the map just proved invertible is the underlying map of $\gamma_N^{A,B}$, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $R_T=A_T$, $S_T=B_T$, and the constant-ring identifications from Step 1. The square of ring maps commutes since all its maps preserve constant sections. That lemma gives the canonical restriction/direct-image comparison and, explicitly, its compatibility with adjoint transposes. Consequently, after forgetting $B$, the transpose of $\gamma_N^{A,B}$ is $\varepsilon_N^A\otimes1_B$ under tensor pullback. Thus the underlying comparison is the ordinary $A$-projection map for $N$ and $B_{\bar X}$.

For clarity write $v_T=\nu_T^*$, $l=p_{\mathrm{et}}^*$, $r=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}^A$, $P=p_{\mathrm{proét}}^*$, $S=Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}^A$. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] supplies $a:v_{\bar X}l\simeq Pv_Y$ and $\beta_H:v_YrH\simeq Sv_{\bar X}H$ with
$$\varepsilon^p\,P(\beta_H)\,a_{rH}=v_{\bar X}(\varepsilon^e_H).$$
It applies to $H=K$ and $H=K\otimes_A^L B$ by Step 3; $p$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Tensor pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies the source and target of $v_Y\pi_K$ with $SN\otimes_A^L B_Y$ and $S(N\otimes_A^L B_{\bar X})$, using these $\beta$'s. Here is the mate calculation explicitly. Put $Q=rK\otimes_A^L B_Y$ and $H=K\otimes_A^L B_{\bar X}$ on the etale sites, and suppress only the canonical tensor-pullback identifications in the following formulas. The resulting map is $t=\beta_H\,v_Y(\pi_K)\,(\beta_K^{-1}\otimes1)$. Its transpose is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^p_{v_{\bar X}H}\,P(t)
&=v_{\bar X}(\varepsilon^e_H)\,a_{rH}^{-1}\,P(v_Y\pi_K)\,P(\beta_K^{-1}\otimes1)\\
&=v_{\bar X}(\varepsilon^e_H\,l\pi_K)\,a_Q^{-1}\,P(\beta_K^{-1}\otimes1)\\
&=\bigl(v_{\bar X}(\varepsilon^e_K)\,a_{rK}^{-1}\,P(\beta_K^{-1})\bigr)\otimes1\\
&=\varepsilon^p_N\otimes1.
\end{aligned}$$
The first and last equalities are the normalization at $H$ and $K$; the second is naturality of $a$ at $\pi_K$; the third uses the defining etale projection transpose $\varepsilon^e_H\,l\pi_K=\varepsilon^e_K\otimes1$ and naturality of tensor pullback. Thus, without suppressed identifications, the transpose is
$$P(SN\otimes_A^L B_Y)\simeq PSN\otimes_A^L B_{\bar X}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_N^p\otimes1}N\otimes_A^L B_{\bar X}.$$
This is exactly the preceding transpose of $\operatorname{Res}\gamma_N^{A,B}$. The adjunction bijection makes the maps equal. As $\pi_K$, both $\beta$'s, and the tensor comparisons are isomorphisms, $\operatorname{Res}\gamma_N^{A,B}$ is an isomorphism. Restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Thus $\gamma_N^{A,B}$ is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$, and Step 2 proves the same for $b_{A,B}(M)$.

source.place: Canonical morphism comparison; blueprint Step 1 normalization, together with sites-cohomology.tex derived tensor/pushforward comparisons

proof.text: Both objects of $b$ have the claimed category membership. The restricted adjunction stated in [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] gives $Rf_{!,A}M\in\Dctf(Y,A)$ and $Rf_{!,B}M_B\in\Dctf(Y,B)$; its finite-commutative-coefficient hypotheses apply to $A$ and $B$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], $(Rf_{!,A}M)_B$ also belongs to $\Dctf(Y,B)$. This is a full subcategory, so the isomorphism already obtained is an isomorphism there. Naturality follows from the explicit counit transpose, tensor comparison, and extension-by-zero maps of Steps 1–2: for $u:M\to M'$ their defining adjuncts agree by naturality of the counit, and hence the corresponding square for $b$ commutes by injectivity of the adjunction bijection.

source.place: Statements of the objects in Dctf and Step 4 naturality

proof.text:
We now prove the coefficient cocycle on the named proper maps. Suppress the pullback/scalar identifications, and identify $T^{B,C}T^{A,B}$ with $T^{A,C}$ by $\alpha$ of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Consider
$$d_N=\gamma^{B,C}_{T^{A,B}N}\circ T_Y^{B,C}(\gamma_N^{A,B}).$$
Its $C$-adjoint transpose, using the defining identity in Step 1 first for $B\to C$ and then for $A\to B$, is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^C\,p_C^*(d_N)
&=T^{B,C}(\varepsilon^B_{T^{A,B}N})\,T^{B,C}(p_B^*\gamma_N^{A,B})\\
&=T^{B,C}\bigl(T^{A,B}(\varepsilon_N^A)\bigr)
 =T^{A,C}(\varepsilon_N^A).
\end{aligned}$$
Naturality of the pullback tensor comparison justifies the first line; its associativity with $\alpha$ is the balancing equality $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes\varphi(b)c$ on K-flat tensor representatives, so the displayed identifications do not change this transpose. The last expression is the defining transpose of $\gamma_N^{A,C}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] therefore gives the proper-map cocycle, including the indicated $\alpha$'s. This calculation takes place for all $N$, so it can be used at $N=j_!M$.

source.place: Step 4, explicit computation of the composed counit transposes

proof.text:
The open tensor maps satisfy the same cocycle. After restriction to $X$, both composites from $T^{B,C}T^{A,B}j_!^AM$ to $j_!^C T^{A,C}M$ give $((m\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto m\otimes\varphi(b)c$. The domain is canonically $j_!^C(T^{B,C}T^{A,B}M)$ by Step 2, and $j_!^C\dashv j^{-1}$ by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. The unit $F\to j^{-1}j_!^CF$ is the identity: in the presheaf construction [def-weil-extension-by-zero], an object $V\to X$ and every object covering it already factor through $X$, so the presheaf and its sheafification restrict to $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. This holds degreewise and hence in the derived categories, since both functors are exact. For $Z=T^{B,C}T^{A,B}M$ the adjunction now identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!^CZ,j_!^CT^{A,C}M)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(Z,T^{A,C}M)$, and sends a map to its restriction. Thus equality after restriction proves equality of the two maps in question. This proves, under $\alpha$, $e_M^{A,C}=e_{T^{A,B}M}^{B,C}\circ T^{B,C}(e_M^{A,B})$.

Finally expand $b=Rp_*(e)\gamma$. Naturality of $\gamma^{B,C}$ with respect to $e_M^{A,B}$ gives, after suppressing the same $\alpha$'s,
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{B,C}(M_B)\,T_Y^{B,C}(b_{A,B}(M))
&=Rp_*^C(e_{M_B}^{B,C})\,\gamma^{B,C}_{j_!^BM_B}\,T_Y^{B,C}(Rp_*^B e_M^{A,B})\,T_Y^{B,C}(\gamma^{A,B}_{j_!^AM})\\
&=Rp_*^C(e_{M_B}^{B,C})\,Rp_*^C(T_{\bar X}^{B,C}e_M^{A,B})\,\gamma^{B,C}_{T^{A,B}j_!^AM}\,T_Y^{B,C}(\gamma^{A,B}_{j_!^AM})\\
&=Rp_*^C(e_M^{A,C})\,\gamma^{A,C}_{j_!^AM}=b_{A,C}(M).
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality uses naturality, and the third uses the open cocycle and Step 8. Reinsert $\alpha$ using its naturality from [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]; the result is exactly the equation in the statement.

Restored the setting explicitly. Removed the out-of-domain A_E,n flat-model invocation, retaining the finite-free/finite-window route through the existing general constant-coefficient etale projection lemma. Added explicit B-linear construction, bounded comparison hypotheses, module/abelian cohomological-dimension bridge, counit normalization, Dctf membership and cocycle computations. No new nodes or Lean work.
